note.title: Reactivity series, displacement and rusting
note.overview: The reactivity series orders metals by how readily they react. It predicts displacement reactions and explains methods used to prevent iron corrosion.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compound; the reverse gives no reaction.
Useful reference order: K, Na, Li, Ca, Mg, Al, (C), Zn, Fe, (H), Cu, Ag, Au.
Carbon and hydrogen are included as reference points even though they are not metals.
Rusting requires iron, oxygen and water.
Barrier methods keep out oxygen/water; galvanising also gives sacrificial protection from zinc.
Oxidation adds oxygen, so a metal sample can gain mass when forming an oxide.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.meaning: an order from more reactive to less reactive substances
a reaction in which a more reactive element replaces a less reactive element in a compound
gain of oxygen in the Year 8 model
gradual destruction of a metal by chemical reactions with its environment
corrosion of iron involving oxygen and water
a coating that blocks water and oxygen
coating iron or steel with zinc
using a more reactive metal that corrodes instead of iron

workedExamples.prompt: Will zinc displace copper from copper sulfate?
workedExamples.answer: Yes. Zinc is more reactive than copper, so zinc sulfate and copper form.
workedExamples.why: Explain chemistry through particles, substances and evidence. Name the particles or substances involved, describe the change or interaction, and connect observations to a balanced scientific explanation.

workedExamples.answer: It forms a barrier that keeps oxygen and water away from the iron.

workedExamples.prompt: Without using options, what does the reactivity series show?
workedExamples.answer: It orders metals from more reactive to less reactive.
workedExamples.why: Key answer: It orders metals from more reactive to less reactive.

workedExamples.prompt: Explain how the series helps predict a reaction between a metal and a metal compound.
workedExamples.answer: Compare the two metals' positions.; The higher/more reactive metal can displace the lower/less reactive one.
workedExamples.why: Key answer: Compare the two metals' positions.; The higher/more reactive metal can displace the lower/less reactive one.

workedExamples.prompt: For Purpose of the reactivity series, a student says: ‘It orders metals only by density.’ Correct the statement and explain the science.
workedExamples.answer: State that the claim is incorrect.; It orders metals from more reactive to less reactive.
workedExamples.why: Key answer: The claim is incorrect. It orders metals from more reactive to less reactive.

commonMistakes: Predicting displacement from which metal has the larger name or mass.
Saying rusting needs carbon dioxide but forgetting water or oxygen.
Claiming paint changes iron into a non-reactive metal.
It orders metals only by density.
Giving a related fact without the defining scientific point.
detailedExplanation: The reactivity series orders metals by how readily they react. It predicts displacement reactions and explains methods used to prevent iron corrosion.

For rusting, name both oxygen and water.
For prevention, state exactly which reactant is blocked or why a sacrificial metal works.
